gameStory.articleHeadline: Emanuel Wilson sparks Seahawks past Chargers 30-23, handing Los Angeles a fourth straight loss
gameStory.articleDescription: — The Seattle Seahawks got their rebound win, but it was far from perfect.
gameStory.articleStory: SEATTLE -- — The Seattle Seahawks got their rebound win, but it was far from perfect. Emanuel Wilson caught a touchdown pass and ran for another score as the Seahawks handed the Los Angeles Chargers a fourth straight loss to start the season with a 30-23 victory on Sunday. Sam Darnold threw for 168 yards and two touchdowns for the defending Super Bowl champions, who are 3-1 after bouncing back from last week's 33-31 loss to the Washington Commanders. But Darnold was also intercepted once and sacked three times. The Seahawks had 14 penalties for a franchise-record 150 yards and they let the Chargers get back in it after leading 27-6 in the third quarter. “We're really grateful for where we're at right now and excited to move forward," Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said. "But we also understand that we have definitely a lot of room for improvement with our operation, how we take care of the football and obviously the penalties are something we need to address.” Wilson rushed for 81 yards on 21 carries and caught three passes for 39 yards. The backup running back, a four-year pro in his first season with the Seahawks, was thrust into a greater role when rookie Jadarian Price was placed on injured reserve on Saturday after aggravating a chest injury during practice. Justin Herbert threw for 189 yards a touchdown and two interceptions for the Chargers (0-4). He has been intercepted six times this season and sacked 12 times, including four for 35 yards on Sunday. whatToWatch.text: Bounce-back at the Clink: Seattle's 2-1 and coming off a loss, laying 7 at home. A defense giving up just 16.7 points a game gets a Chargers offense down three bodies — including Ladd McConkey. That's the recipe for getting right.

Low total, high stakes: the 42.5 over/under screams grind-it-out. Both teams average 2.3 sacks a game, but LAC is surrendering 25.3 points per game while Seattle gives up 16.7 — if the Hawks win the field-position fight, this one tilts fast.

Depth gets tested: three Seahawks are out (Jadarian Price, Ty Okada, Chazz Surratt) with two more questionable. Good news — the Chargers are without Dalvin Tomlinson up front, so there's room to run and a chance for next-man-up guys to make their mark.

recap.text: Seattle forced three Chargers turnovers and turned them into points, building a lead Los Angeles never erased in a 30-23 win at home. Sam Darnold threw touchdowns to Emanuel Wilson and Tory Horton, Wilson punched one in on the ground, and Rashid Shaheed ripped off a 28-yard scoring run — enough cushion to survive a missed extra point from Jason Myers. The Chargers clawed back in the second half behind a Justin Herbert touchdown pass to Kimani Vidal and an Omarion Hampton plunge, trimming it to one score with Cameron Dicker's late field goal. But Seattle's defense slammed the door, and the Seahawks walked off with a seven-point victory.

newsBlurb.text: Seattle limps home from Washington carrying a rare loss, one built on a stalled running game and three turnovers that handed the Commanders 21 points — exactly the sloppiness Mike Macdonald's group has to scrub before the Chargers arrive. The secondary could get reinforcements: Julian Love, sidelined by a calf injury suffered in practice, drew a "day to day" tag from Macdonald after encouraging Monday work. How the offense reestablishes the run will shape everything else in this one.
